items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: The interviewer addresses the interviewee as 'Pontch', which is a nickname for Ernest 'Punch' Miller. The transcript contains no mention of a separate person named 'Pontch'.

ctx.x: Yeah. Yeah. This was in forty, forty, one I think. That's when I quit drinking. Yeah, that's forty-one. Mm-hmm.
Forty-one. Well, I was wondering about it, Pontch. Let me fix that machine there. When were you in Springfield? Right.

Well, I was there with a fellow named Oliver Bibbs. That was late after, way after me and Francois and them broke up. That's where I must have been in. It must have been around thirty, oh, not no thirty. Around about, 45 or something like that. 46, 47, around that day. Long after you'd stopped drinking then. Yeah. Oh yeah, I quit drinking altogether.
